PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  ACTION SUMMARY
  March 19, 2024, COMMISSION MEETING

Commission Members Present: Larry Giannone (Chair), Bob Olander, Karol Curtis, Patrick
Jones, Orlando Pimental, Greg Tober, Ruth Luevand
Commission Members Absent:
City Representatives: City Manager Chris Constantin, Sr. Management Analyst Anissa Livas

 ORAL COMMUNICATIONS  COMMENTS/RECOMMENDATIONS
  None

 BUSINESS ITEMS  COMMENTS/RECOMMENDATIONS
 BI.1 Approval of Minutes for November 21,  Motion by Patrick Jones and seconded by
 2023 (City Manager Chris Constantin)  Orlando Pimental to approve the minutes of
  January 16, 2024. (Passed 7-0).

 BI.2 Discussion of Part 1 Crimes for January  Captain Ashrafnia provided an update on part 1
 2024 Compared with January 2023 (Captain  crime statistics for January 2024 as compared
 Walid Ashrafnia)  to January 2023. Crime was down 21.8% from
  the month last year. Across the board, crime
  was down in multiple areas.

  LASD held a community meeting with the
  Community Action Team for the Via Verde
  Ridge HOA with over 60 residents.
  Discussions were positive about how we can
  continue to reduce crime in the area. Captain
  Ashrafnia encouraged commissioners to
  request community meetings where desired to
  help educate the public on what they can do to
  reduce the potential for crime.
 March 19, 2024 Public Safety Commission Minutes  Page 2

  Commissioners discussed the impact of
  squatters on one property, and the generally
  discussed how does the City and LASD combat
  this problem.

 BI.3 Discussion of on the Municipal Law  City Manager Constantin advised the
 Enforcement Services Agreement (City  commission on the progress of the new 5-year
 Manager Chris Constantin)  Municipal Law Enforcement Services
  Agreement. Constantin walked through a
  typical monthly invoice from the County for
  law enforcement services including the
  itemized listing of positions, deployment, and
  costs associated with positions and equipment.

  Constantin updated the increase estimated for
  the 2024-25 agreement to be 3.56% from the
  2023-24 cost for services. He also updated the
  commission on how liability claims are
  navigated and the role of the Liability Trust
  Fund Claims Board in reviewing and settling
  claims. The discussion also involved when a
  claim would be a City claim versus a County
  claim.
 BI.4 Discussion of on the Use of Private  City Manager Constantin highlighted the
 Security Patrol to Augment Public Safety  program implemented in the City of Lakewood
 Services – City of Lakewood (City Manager  to augment public safety by the addition of
 Chris Constantin)  non-sworn private security.

  Lakewood acquired non-sworn service because
  they are not able to obtain more deputies due to
  a freeze from the County on adding new items
  to a City’s contract.
 NEW BUSINESS ITEMS  COMMENTS/RECOMMENDATIONS
 R1 Commissioner Reports  Orlando Pimental – Pimental thanked staff as
  he feels safer from what he is seeing the City
  and LASD doing. Pimental highlighted the
  need to improve opportunities to enhance bike
  safety on our streets, specifically San Dimas
  Avenue by the rail tracks.

  Patrick Jones – Jones added to Pimental’s
  update on bike safety. If the City discusses
  drones, I would like to be involved in the
  discussion.
 March 19, 2024 Public Safety Commission Minutes  Page 3

  Bob Olander – Olander appreciates the focus
  the City makes of public safety. Public safety
  will be priority one over the next few years.

  Ruth Luevand – Luevand thanked staff for
  doing research into A.I and highlighted an
  analytics system in Australia that uses
  geospatial mapping data that tracks persons
  that would be at risk of being a victim.
  Residents can sign up for this

  Karol Curtis – Curtis sees a lot of people
  walking in the downtown, and we are a
  walkable area in downtown. Thanked staff for
  a wonderful San Dimas Booster event for
  volunteers at the station

  Greg Tobar – Tobar continues to highlight the
  benefit of Flock cameras, our license reading
  program. Tobar was concerned about traffic
  safety.

 R2 Station Captain’s Report (Captain  Captain Ashrafnia informed the commission
 Ashrafnia)  that they want to educate the public to use their
  new Online Reporting Systems (SORTS) that
  allows residents to report certain crimes.

 R3 City Staff Liaison Report (City Manager  The City Manager updated the commission on
 Chris Constantin)  our future planned dam visit. He also updated
  the commission on the City budget as well as
  the City Resident survey. Constantin also
  highlighted that we want to do things well and
  it includes doing less in a better way. Traffic
  safety is also important, so Constantin
  highlighted the new traffic capability added to
  the Community Action Team which included
  LIDAR speed devices.

The meeting adjourned at 7:14 PM.
